quote: Amended §11.2 (via Amendment §2.1) excludes from the cap only: (a) Supplier's indemnity obligation under §9.1, "which are excluded solely to third-party intellectual property claims under Section 9.1(c)" ... Recall costs (§10) are no longer carved out — they are now subject to the cap. ... For a beverage bottler, the two most catastrophic risks are (1) a product recall caused by defective containers ... and (2) personal injury to consumers. Both are now subject to the six-month payment cap.
reason: The memo correctly identifies that the Amendment replaces Supply Agreement §11.2. It explains that the replacement removes recall costs from the carve-outs and limits the indemnity carve-out to third-party IP claims. It also explains that recall and product-liability exposure is now capped at six months of fees. The memo cites the provision as §2.1 rather than Section 2, but this is a minor citation difference; the substance matches the criterion. It also notes that the amendment controls under §15.2 and recommends restoring the original §11.2.
